| [THEORY-030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-030.md) v4 | Landauer prices only losing distinguishability | Bennett (2003), [LIT-360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-360.md): the cost attaches to many-to-one maps of the logical state, at least k ln 2 of entropy per bit exported to non-information-bearing degrees of freedom, which "need not" be heat. | [THEORY-072](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md) v5 | Organisms differ from flames by differentiation | The record's first answer to the demarcation question that [NOTE-094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-094.md) reports. Mossio, Saborido & Moreno (2009, [LIT-570](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-570.md)) grant a candle flame organisational closure. Its one macroscopic pattern keeps up the conditions of the combustion that makes it. They draw the line at organisational differentiation: in an organism several distinct structures make distinct contributions, where a flame makes "a unique contribution". Montévil & Mossio (2015, [LIT-582](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-582.md)) narrow closure to mutual dependence among constraints. Each constraint must be both produced by and productive of another, with at least one slow and one fast dependence. On the record's reading, that builds differentiation into closure, as Mossio and Bich (2014) already say of closure of constraints. No paper analyses a flame under the 2015 definitions. Neither paper says closure defines an organism. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-128](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-128.md) | Coral recovery needs herbivores to curb algae | Hughes et al. (2007), [LIT-711](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-711.md). On the reef crest at Orpheus Island after the 1998 bleaching, four roofless cages kept large and medium fishes out of 25 m² plots for 30 months. Macroalgae averaged 56% cover inside against 4.1% and 1.7% in controls. Coral cover reached 7.7% inside against 19.2% and 20.2%, with recruitment about two-thirds lower and mortality of established colonies more than double. Control recovery came mainly from recruits of taxa bleaching had removed. Proposed: one site, four replicates, plot scale, and fish exclusion standing in for herbivore exclusion. The algal state vanished within 30 days of reopening. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-129](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-129.md) | Coral spawning needs the natural night light | Kaniewska et al. (2015), [LIT-710](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-710.md), at Heron Island. In 2011, colonies under natural night light spawned with the reef, while colonies lit after sunset or kept dark for the preceding week did not spawn that night (N = 6, 5, 5). 184 transcripts changed around release in ambient colonies, early in lit ones and not at all in dark ones, and the induced genes were enriched for G-protein-coupled signalling. In 2006, blue, green or white nocturnal light delayed spawning 6–8 h or two nights and red did not. Proposed: one species and site, small groups, and a cascade inferred from co-expression. It shows synchrony by a shared cue, not coupling between colonies. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-408](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-408.md) v3 | Gene frequencies track inclusive fitness | Hamilton (1964), Part I, [LIT-497](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-497.md), read in full in [NOTE-401](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-401.md). Each effect an individual causes falls partly on genes identical by descent with its own (weight r) and partly on others, which only dilute. So selection tracks inclusive fitness. The threshold is written −k > 1/r (§5), not rb > c: "more than two brothers, or four half-brothers, or eight first cousins". The maximization theorem needs non-negative total effects on others; for harming traits the change only points uphill. r is exact only for loci not under selection, and Hamilton could not bound the error (§4). | Active |
| [THEORY-431](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-431.md) v2 | Crooks symmetry holds for entropy production | Crooks (1999), [LIT-522](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-522.md), read in [NOTE-413](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-413.md), with Jarzynski (1997), [LIT-517](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-517.md) ([NOTE-417](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-417.md)), and Seifert's review (2012), [LIT-523](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-523.md) ([NOTE-420](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-420.md)). The work equality ⟨e^{−βW}⟩ = e^{−βΔF} holds at any switching rate, and Crooks derives it from a trajectory-level entropy-production theorem; Seifert derives every known theorem of the kind from one master theorem. These are exact given their premises. They are not proofs of the second law, since the dynamics build irreversibility in, and they say nothing about extremum principles for steady states. Their practical reach is work fluctuations of order k_BT. | Active |

| [THEORY-466](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-466.md) v2 | Hawk isn't stable; conventional fighting can be | Maynard Smith & Price (1973), [LIT-505](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-505.md), read in full in [NOTE-404](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-404.md). | [THEORY-473](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-473.md) | Individual niche is mostly counterfactual | Takola & Schielzeth (2022), [LIT-127](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-127.md), read in full in [NOTE-170](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-170.md). The working definition (p. 5) gives the individualized niche an absolute-fitness boundary, expected LRS ≥ 1, and splits it into realized, potential, time-slice, prospective and trajectory-based niches. That the realized niche is a point and the potential niche unobservable follows from the definitions. The paper concedes there is "no empirical solution" at the individual level (p. 15), and its fix, marginalizing fitness functions across individuals, is schematic. | [THEORY-499](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-499.md) v2 | Eulalia breakup may have made 800 Ma craters | Bottke, Vokrouhlický, Dykhuis & Zellner (2026), [LIT-009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-009.md), read in full in [NOTE-002](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-002.md). | [THEORY-543](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-543.md) v2 | Diffusion can destabilise a stable steady state | Turing (1952), [LIT-535](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-535.md), read in full in [NOTE-427](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-427.md), with Cross & Hohenberg (1993), [LIT-527](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-527.md), skimmed in [NOTE-418](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-418.md). | [THEORY-562](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-562.md) | REST2 replica mixing doesn't show sampling | Koneru, Reid & Robustelli (2025), [LIT-076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-076.md), read in full in [NOTE-076](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-076.md). | [THEORY-567](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-567.md) | Five mechanisms each stabilise cooperation | Nowak (2006), [LIT-501](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-501.md), read in [NOTE-409](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-409.md), main text only. A four-page review that casts each known mechanism as a 2×2 game so that one set of criteria applies to all. The five ESS conditions are confirmed by the main text; the derivations are in the supporting material, which was not read, and in cited papers. Several rules hold only under weak selection, regular graphs or rare group splitting. Every mechanism is modelled with the donation game, so mutualism, coordination and conflict are outside it. | Active |

| [THEORY-663](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-663.md) | Reciprocal altruism can evolve between non-kin | Trivers (1971), [LIT-510](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-510.md), read in full in [NOTE-402](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-402.md). | [THEORY-672](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-672.md) v2 | TIT FOR TAT is stable when w is high enough | Axelrod & Hamilton (1981), [LIT-498](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-498.md), read in full in [NOTE-411](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-411.md). Against TIT FOR TAT the best reply is always-defect or alternation, which gives the condition on w. The cluster result and the "ratchet" are explicit payoff comparisons. "Evolutionarily stable" here means no mutant does better, which is weaker than Maynard Smith and Price's definition: always cooperate does exactly as well. The model is deterministic and error-free. Tournament robustness is a separate, empirical claim about the strategies people submitted. | Active |
| [THEORY-679](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-679.md) v2 | Replication heat grows with durability, not info | England (2012; J. Chem. Phys. 2013), [LIT-515](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-515.md), read in [NOTE-419](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-419.md). The general bound, β⟨ΔQ⟩ + ln π(II→I) + ΔS_int ≥ 0, is a coarse-grained second law and was re-derived. Applied to replication it gives a heat cost of about 2n ln(n τ_decay/τ_div) per copy, which falls away as division slows. The numbers for E. coli (within a factor of three of the bound) and RNA rest on an upper bound on the reverse probability that is argued from biology, not proved, and on an internal-entropy term set "arbitrarily". It prices finite-time irreversibility, not information, and draws no line between living and non-living replicators. | Active |
| [THEORY-682](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-682.md) | Two-stage cascade can read signal frequency | Folz, Wettmann, Morigi & Kruse (2018; PRE 2019), [LIT-034](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-034.md), read in full in [NOTE-067](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-067.md). The period independence is proved, for signals that differ by a time rescaling only; the two-stage readout is shown numerically and in the Heaviside limit; the loop's minimum length and ω ≈ √3 v/L for long axons come from linear stability analysis. The length control is a lumped delay-differential model with one parameter set and the motor velocity v never stated, so its absolute lengths, about 125 µm, cannot be reproduced. A proof of mechanism, not a model fitted to axons. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-742](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-742.md) v3 | Coarse-graining keeps the metric's singular part | Raju, Machta and Sethna (2018), [LIT-1254](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1254.md), read in [NOTE-972](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-972.md). The loss identity holds for any coarse-graining of an exponential family; that the loss is analytic, and so spares the singular part of the metric, needs an exact renormalization step with linear beta functions and an analytic constant. It does not say that relevant directions keep their information in general: on the paper's own scalings only directions with RG eigenvalue above d/2 do, and away from the Gaussian fixed point even the drift loses information. | Active |
| [THEORY-747](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-747.md) | Finite-memory MZ closure rivals Smagorinsky | Parish and Duraisamy (2017), [LIT-1259](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1259.md), read in [NOTE-973](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-973.md). The closure is [THEORY-760](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-760.md)'s finite Markovian augmentation. Here is how it did, as far as the paper's plots show: close to filtered DNS in integral quantities, comparable to dynamic Smagorinsky in equilibrium turbulence, clearly better on a transitional flow, and with the subgrid transfer peaked at the cutoff where DNS puts it but about 40% too deep. The paper calls the predictions "excellent" with no numbers. Its fitted memory length shortens as the resolved dynamics speed up, so the memory belongs to the cutoff as much as to the flow. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-748](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-748.md) | Signed entropy rate doesn't detect cascades | Granero-Belinchón, Roux and Garnier (2016), [LIT-1243](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1243.md), read in [NOTE-970](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-970.md), claim that conditioning the entropy rate on the sign of the increment lets one "prove the existence of the energy cascade" using information theory. The record finds two limits. The unconditioned entropy rate is exactly blind to reflection and time reversal. The conditioned one detects any central asymmetry of the two-point law, including one with no increment skewness at all. Independent pairs with the paper's one-point skewness of 0.175 give h⁺ − h⁻ ≈ 0.066 nats with symmetric increments. Nothing in the paper ties an information quantity to the energy balance. | Active |
| [THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md) v4 | Euler solutions above 1/3 conserve energy | Constantin, E and Titi (1994), [LIT-1248](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1248.md), read in [NOTE-982](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-982.md). The positive half of Onsager's conjecture, in the Besov form: if velocity increments obey ‖u(·+y) − u‖_{L³} ≤ C\|y\|^α with α > 1/3, integrated in time, the coarse-grained energy flux across scale ε is O(ε^(3α−1)) and no energy can be lost to vanishing scales. It is a statement about regular fields only. It does not show that a flux survives the limit for rougher ones: that energy can fail to be conserved below 1/3 is Isett's later theorem ([THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md)), that it can strictly decrease is Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi and Vicol's (THEORY-776), both Proposed, and some rough solutions conserve energy anyway. | Active |
| [THEORY-750](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-750.md) | Information scaling is structure-function scaling | Granero-Belinchón, Roux and Garnier (2016), [LIT-1243](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1243.md), read in full in [NOTE-970](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-970.md). A Gaussian identity and its small-lag asymptotics: the conditional entropy of x(t) given x(t − τ) is a monotone function of the autocorrelation, so its scaling exponent is half the structure-function exponent. In the Modane data the estimated entropy rate matches the Gaussian formula, so the measured "information spectrum" is S₂ again. It is not a distribution of a conserved quantity over scales, and it carries nothing about the direction or size of energy transfer. It answers [QUESTION-219](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-219.md) only in the narrow sense of supporting A3's caution. | Active |
| [THEORY-752](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-752.md) | t-model memory acts as growing damping | Chorin, Hald and Kupferman (2002), [LIT-1253](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1253.md), read in [NOTE-975](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-975.md): Theorem 8.1. Truncating the Mori–Zwanzig memory integral at its lag-zero value gives dΦ/dt = R̄(Φ) + tS(Φ), and under the stated conditions this dissipates the free energy of the resolved variables. It says nothing about how well the t-model predicts, gives no error bound, and holds only for the conditional-expectation projection; the true conditional mean's effective energy need not decrease. | Active |
| [THEORY-754](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-754.md) v3 | Energy transfer is local in scale | Eyink and Aluie (2009), [LIT-1239](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1239.md), read in [NOTE-969](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-969.md), stating bounds proved in Eyink (2005), [LIT-1252](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1252.md). A conditional inequality: if velocity increments scale no faster than r^σ in the L³ mean, the contributions of far larger and far smaller scales to the mean flux across ℓ are bounded by powers of the scale ratio. It needs 0 < σ < 1: σ < 1 for the large scales, σ > 0 for the small. That the inertial range satisfies the hypothesis, that the mean flux there is non-zero, and the sharper 4/3 exponent are assumptions or heuristics, not part of it. It is about one field decomposed by scale, and says nothing about units. | Active |
| [THEORY-760](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-760.md) | Finite-memory MZ closure is Markovian, inexact | Parish and Duraisamy (2017), [LIT-1259](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1259.md), read in [NOTE-973](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-973.md). The finite-memory closure turns the Mori–Zwanzig memory integral into auxiliary ordinary differential equations, so the reduced model is the resolved variables plus finitely many memory coordinates: the shape of augmentation [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md) asks about. But the truncation drops the next auxiliary term without a bound, the memory length is fitted, and the kernel's form is fixed by the quadrature, not by the eliminated dynamics. It is an augmentation with uncontrolled error, not the controlled one the question asks for. | Active |
| [THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md) v2 | Euler solutions below 1/3 can dissipate | Isett (2018), [LIT-1255](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1255.md), skimmed in [NOTE-974](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-974.md): the negative half of Onsager's conjecture. With [THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md) (Constantin, E and Titi, the positive half) it makes 1/3 the threshold. For the record, its point is that below 1/3 the energy flux into vanishing scales can survive the limit, which is the half of A3's point that THEORY-749 could not give. It does not say that this flux is a dissipative cascade. Isett's solutions start from rest, gain energy and lose it again, so the surviving flux takes both signs. Nor does it say that such solutions are limits of Navier–Stokes or describe turbulence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-772](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-772.md) v2 | Euler solutions can confine dissipation to pipes | Giri, Kwon and Novack (2023; Annals 2026), [LIT-1289](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1289.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1022](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1022.md): the L³-based strong Onsager theorem. Below 1/3, in Constantin, E and Titi's own scale of spaces ([THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md)), there are weak Euler solutions satisfying the local energy inequality. In the proof the Duchon–Robert measure is a prescribed smooth function, positive in a periodic array of pipes and zero elsewhere. So the coarse-grained flux into vanishing scales is one-signed locally in space and time, in the limit, and not only for the whole box as in [THEORY-776](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-776.md). Its location and rate are inputs of the construction; it is a smooth density on a few pipes, not concentrated on a thin set; nothing is said about the sign at a positive scale or about vanishing viscosity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-774](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-774.md) | Hopping-model Fisher eigenvalues split by factor t | Machta, Chachra, Transtrum and Sethna (2013), [LIT-1299](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1299.md), supplement §III, read in [NOTE-1018](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1018.md). The eigenvalues grow for particle creation (t^(3/2)) and drift (t^(1/2)) and fall from the diffusion constant on (t^(−1/2), t^(−3/2), …). The data are not a coarse-graining of one fixed data set, so nothing forbids growth. The metric is a least-squares metric with an arbitrary unit of error, and its eigenvalues depend on the coordinates θ_μ. The ratio between successive eigenvalues matches the 1/n per Hermite order of [THEORY-742](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-742.md)'s diffusion result, though the two set-ups differ. | Active |
| [THEORY-776](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-776.md) v3 | Euler solutions can follow any decreasing energy | Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi and Vicol (2017; CPAM 2019), [LIT-1300](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1300.md), read in [NOTE-1013](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1013.md): the admissible version of Isett's negative half of Onsager's conjecture ([THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md)). Any smooth positive energy profile can be imposed on a C^β solution, β < 1/3, so a strictly decreasing one gives solutions whose total energy only falls. Through [THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md)'s energy balance, the coarse-grained flux then runs into the vanishing scales on every time interval. That is the one-way transfer [THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md) could not give. It is one-way for the box as a whole, not at every point (no local energy inequality is proved); the same theorem gives increasing energy as readily, so the direction is a choice of the construction; and nothing ties these solutions to Navier–Stokes, to a constant-flux inertial range or to uniqueness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-777](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-777.md) | Decimation keeps only relevant Fisher directions | Machta, Chachra, Transtrum and Sethna (2013), [LIT-1299](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1299.md), Fig. 3, read in [NOTE-1018](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1018.md). One lattice size, one temperature, at most six steps of b = √2 (so b^n ≤ 8), no error bars, and no fitted rates. The groups and their rates are bands the authors drew. The value y = 0 is not an operator of the 2D Ising model: it is the rate at which any direction without singular support loses information as sites are discarded. The caption's rate 2^(−d−y) disagrees with the bands and with the supplement's b^(2y−d). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-780](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-780.md) | Transcriptional regulation alone can store memory | Zhao, Wytock, Reynolds and Motter (2024), [LIT-854](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-854.md), read in full in [NOTE-655](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-655.md). Their abstract and discussion carry the model result to cells: one genotype may hold several heritable expression states without epigenetic marks, and history picks among them. They predict that a transient crp knockdown leaves zraR, melR or rhaRS changed ([NOTE-655](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-655.md), C8, untested). [THEORY-178](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-178.md) is the model result this rests on. No such perturbation has been done in cells ([QUESTION-172](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-172.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-789](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-789.md) | Max-information coarse-graining finds RG variables | Koch-Janusz and Ringel (2017), [LIT-873](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md), propose that their mutual-information criterion finds a system's relevant degrees of freedom with no prior knowledge of them. What the record holds as shown, [THEORY-194](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-194.md), is that it recovered variables renormalization already uses, on 2D models whose answer was known. This is the general thesis that result was offered for, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-817](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-817.md) | Max prediction isn't max work under feedback | Fiderer et al. (2025), [LIT-041](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-041.md), read in [NOTE-032](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-032.md), prove that without feedback the work-efficient agents are exactly the maximally predictive ones that randomise and forget their actions, and that with feedback one binary memoryless channel separates predictive, max-entropy-action and efficient agents; from that they assert that with feedback maximally predictive agents are generally inefficient. The record holds as proved, in [THEORY-026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md), only the one channel. It does not say that efficiency under feedback is a trade-off between prediction and forgetting: in the proved example the efficient agent is memoryless. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-818](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-818.md) v4 | NARMAX closure doubles Lorenz 96 forecast lead | Chorin and Lu (2015), [LIT-1304](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1304.md), read in [NOTE-1028](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1028.md). A data-driven closure with one or two steps of discrete memory, plus one moving-average innovation, is enough on this test to reproduce the resolved statistics and to double forecast skill against a memoryless-in-x closure. It is the record's first evidence that a short discrete memory suffices in a chaotic system with no scale gap. It is one system, the structure was tuned, and there is no bound, so it does not give the controlled prediction error [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md) asks for. | Active |
| [THEORY-821](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-821.md) | Locally dissipative Euler solutions exist, α<1/15 | Isett (2017; ARMA 2022), [LIT-1305](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1305.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1027](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1027.md): the first continuous, indeed C^α with α < 1/15, weak Euler solutions satisfying the local energy inequality with nonzero dissipation, and a Cantor family of them sharing one initial datum and one dissipation measure. In the construction the dissipation measure is a function of time alone, so in the limit of vanishing scale the energy flux runs one way at every place, as in [THEORY-772](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-772.md), but in a Hölder class and spread uniformly over the torus rather than set in pipes. It is switched on only while the constructor drains the solution's energy to zero at the end of its life. Where, when and how fast the energy goes are inputs; the exponent is far from 1/3; nothing ties these solutions to Navier–Stokes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1008](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1008.md) | MMSB memberships predict protein function | Airoldi, Blei, Fienberg and Xing (2008), [LIT-1553](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1553.md), §4.3.2 and Figs. 10–12, read in [NOTE-1179](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1179.md). The batch's one check of inferred mixed memberships against labels the model never saw. The reported margin is over a weak baseline, so it shows less than it seems: probably some information, not yet how much. It says nothing about whether the fifteen blocks are the fifteen functions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1049](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1049.md) v3 | Tiny symbionts lose envelope, then translation | McCutcheon, Garber, Spencer & Warren (2024), [LIT-1571](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1571.md), read in [NOTE-1213](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1213.md). The envelope goes first, near 400 kb, and translation starts to go below about 200 kb, the authors' "tipping point". Such symbionts have three-membrane envelopes and among the most biased proteomes in bacteria. They can only work if the host provides what they no longer encode. The host's role is inferred, not shown: the mechanisms are, in the paper's word, mysteries. | Active |
| [THEORY-1085](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1085.md) v2 | Flock order is a broken continuous symmetry | Toner and Tu (1995), [LIT-1670](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1670.md), read in [NOTE-1228](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1228.md) from the arXiv preprint. Active as a statement of what the theory is: its variables, the degree of freedom it eliminates and why, and the modes that remain, all in the text (pp. 3–8). It does not say that the theory's exponents are right ([THEORY-1095](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1095.md)), that the universality claim holds, or that the order so described is an agent or an individual. | Active |
| [THEORY-1095](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1095.md) | Flocks keep long-range order in 2D | Toner and Tu (1995), [LIT-1670](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1670.md), read in [NOTE-1228](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1228.md) from the arXiv preprint. The linear theory's loss of order in d ≤ 2 and the relevance of the convective nonlinearity below d = 4 are calculations. The survival of order in d = 2 follows from χ = −1/5 < 0, which is exact only if a cubic vertex stays irrelevant ("we strongly suspect"), or from χ = (z − d)/3 with z < 2, which is expected "on physical grounds". The change-of- neighbours mechanism is a heuristic. Proposed for those two steps. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1098](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1098.md) v2 | Mitochondrion lost only after functions moved | Karnkowska et al. (2019), [LIT-1574](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1574.md), read in [NOTE-1243](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1243.md). The SUF replacement of the mitochondrial Fe–S pathway is shared by all examined Preaxostyla, including relatives that keep a mitochondrion-related organelle, and those relatives' organelle still houses the glycine cleavage system that M. exilis lacks. So the organelle lost its jobs in at least two steps before it was lost. Apart from the mitochondrion, peroxisomes and mitophagy, the cell's systems are those of an ordinary eukaryote. The order is inferred, not dated, and absence is limited by annotation. | Active |
| [THEORY-1099](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1099.md) v3 | Host complexity predates the mitochondrion | Kay et al. (2026), [LIT-1566](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1566.md), read in [NOTE-1234](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1234.md). A dated species tree places nFECA at 3.05–2.79 Ga, mFECA at 2.37–2.13 Ga and LECA at 1.80–1.67 Ga. Against an endosymbiosis marker at about 2.2 Ga, 85% of archaeal-origin duplications are older, and most non-alphaproteobacterial bacterial duplications are younger. The authors reject mitochondria-early scenarios and argue against serial endosymbiosis. The sharp edges are that duplication dates bound functions from above, that the priors shape which family can be older, and that the authors themselves cannot order phagocytosis and the mitochondrion. | Active |
| [THEORY-1100](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1100.md) v2 | Integration needs no endosymbiont gene transfer | Sørensen, Stiller, Kröninger & Nowack (2025), [LIT-1560](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1560.md), read in [NOTE-1241](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1241.md). Protein mass spectrometry of isolated endosymbionts found hundreds of host proteins imported into Paulinella's chromatophore and more than 350 into the nitroplast, where they fill gaps left by lost genes. In Paulinella the imported proteins come mostly from the host's own genes, with some from gene transfer from the chromatophore and from other bacteria. In the nitroplast no gene transfer from the symbiont has been found at all. So the route to an organelle is import, and the endosymbiont's genes need not move. The origins are stated in summary, not counted, and the import mechanisms are unknown. | Active |
| [THEORY-1101](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1101.md) v3 | Stem length is not an acquisition clock | Tobiasson, Luo, Wolf & Koonin (2026), [LIT-1558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1558.md), read in [NOTE-1242](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1242.md). They test the stem-length method of Pittis and Gabaldón on their own trees and reproduce its mitochondrion-late signal only for long stems. Below 0.3, where 70% of stems lie, the order reverses, and genes presumably acquired together scatter widely. They conclude that "even normalized stem lengths are determined primarily by factors other than the gene acquisition time". The paper still favours a late mitochondrion, on other grounds. | Active |
| [THEORY-1102](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1102.md) v2 | Mitochondria arrived late to a chimaeric host | Pittis & Gabaldón (2016), [LIT-1595](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1595.md), read in [NOTE-1240](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1240.md). Of 1,078 LECA families, bacterial ones have shorter normalized stems than archaeal ones (P = 1.38e-25), and alphaproteobacterial ones shorter than other bacterial ones (P = 0.044). Origin tracks location: alphaproteobacterial with the mitochondrion, other bacterial with endomembranes, archaeal with the nucleus. A plastid control runs the right way. The sharp edges are that stem length measures distance to the closest sampled relative, so sampling can move it, and that the chimaeric host could have come from partners or from transfer, which the paper cannot tell apart. | Active |
| [THEORY-1103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1103.md) v2 | Buchnera keeps only what its host lacks | Shigenobu et al. (2000), [LIT-1596](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1596.md), read in [NOTE-1236](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1236.md). The first complete genome of an obligate insect endosymbiont: 640,681 bp, a subset of E. coli's. What is shown is gene content. The interlocking of host and symbiont metabolism is inferred from it and from earlier physiology. That Buchnera cannot live outside the bacteriocyte, and that the host supplies its membrane lipids, are the authors' inferences. The paper names no mechanism of loss beyond a homeostatic niche: it says nothing of drift. | Active |
| [THEORY-1104](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1104.md) v3 | Asgard is the largest eukaryotic gene source | Tobiasson, Luo, Wolf & Koonin (2026), [LIT-1558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1558.md), read in [NOTE-1242](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1242.md). In 4,290 well-resolved eukaryotic–prokaryotic clusters, Asgard takes 50% of likelihood weight and leads in almost every functional class. Alphaproteobacteria account for mitochondrial translation, oxidative phosphorylation and 4Fe-4S assembly. About a third of clusters point elsewhere, with no functional pattern except a narrow Myxococcota signal. The authors infer a complex Asgard ancestor, a late mitochondrion and "no indication of another symbiotic event". The composition is shown; the scenario is read off it. | Active |
| [THEORY-1105](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1105.md) v3 | LECA acquired partners in serial waves | Bernabeu, Manzano-Morales, Marcet-Houben & Gabaldón (2026), [LIT-1561](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1561.md), read in [NOTE-1237](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1237.md). Under thresholds chosen to maximize assignments to Alphaproteobacteria and Asgard, Myxococcota (3.92% of the proteome) and Planctomycetota (2.24%) pass in every dataset, beside Alphaproteobacteria (3.99%) and Asgard (3.28%). A control removing Alphaproteobacteria from the database does not reproduce their pattern. Stem lengths put Planctomycetota before the mitochondrion. The authors "challenge models depicting eukaryogenesis as a one-off event resulting from a binary symbiotic interaction", and also say their data "do not provide information on the host or endosymbiotic nature of any partner". | Active |
| [THEORY-1106](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1106.md) v2 | Hosts raise titre for fragmented Hodgkinia | Campbell, Łukasik, Meyer, Buckner, Simon, Veloso, Michalik & McCutcheon (2018), [LIT-1590](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1590.md), read in [NOTE-1235](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1235.md). Measured: Hodgkinia cells per egg from 4,889 in a single-lineage cicada to 30,154 in M. septendecim, with Sulcia at 2,572 to 5,643; marker genotypes present in every egg sampled; the same route under the light microscope. Not shown: a trend across complexity beyond M. septendecim, or that splitting came first. The authors also speculate that a larger transmitted population weakens bottlenecks and could feed further splitting. | Active |
| [THEORY-1107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1107.md) v2 | Organelles arise stepwise via protein import | Sørensen, Stiller, Kröninger & Nowack (2025), [LIT-1560](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1560.md), read in [NOTE-1241](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1241.md). Their closing scenario orders the steps from endosymbiont to organelle: effectors first, then dependence through one redundant imported protein, then many imported proteins once a targeting signal evolves. Rhizobia, targeted by about 700 host peptides yet not vertically transmitted, are their case of control without integration. It is a scenario built from systems at different stages, not a sequence observed in any one. | Active |
| [THEORY-1108](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1108.md) v2 | Asgard ancestor was likely syntrophic | Imachi et al. (2020), [LIT-1591](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1591.md), read in [NOTE-1238](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1238.md). Partner inhibitors impair MK-D1's growth, added hydrogen or formate stops it, and it grows with either of two methanogens, so its dependence is on a service that several partners can supply. Cryo-EM and TEM show no internal compartments. The step from this one organism to the Asgard ancestor is a genomic inference, which the authors hedge. The sharp edge for the record is that the most famous transition in individuality may have begun from a host already dependent on others, with no partner specificity, cohesion or control. | Active |
| [THEORY-1109](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1109.md) v3 | LECA central carbon metabolism was chimeric | Santana-Molina, Williams, Snel & Spang (2025), [LIT-1564](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1564.md), read in [NOTE-1239](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1239.md). LECA had a complete central carbon metabolism. Six enzymes are placed with Asgard archaea, mostly cytosolic (bootstrap 39–97%, two ambiguous). Seventeen are alphaproteobacterial, ten of them in the TCA cycle, mostly mitochondrial. Others come from several bacteria, none dominant. Since LECA, Asgard enzymes have been replaced in many lineages and enzymes retargeted regardless of origin. The authors read the split as support for syntrophy; it does not discriminate syntrophy from other symbiogenetic models. | Active |

| [THEORY-1411](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1411.md) v2 | Creased sheet can learn to classify forces | Stern, Arinze, Perez, Palmer and Murugan (2020; arXiv 2019), [LIT-2116](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2116.md), read in [NOTE-1615](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1615.md) from the arXiv v1 preprint, titled differently; the PNAS text and the Supplementary Notes were not read. Proposed for that reason. It is a result about a model: it does not say that any physical sheet has been trained, that the sheet learns without an external supervisor, or that it scales beyond small two-class tasks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1414](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1414.md) v3 | Prestress redirects forces exciting zero modes | Rocks and Mehta (2024; arXiv 2022), [LIT-2112](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2112.md), read in full in [NOTE-1557](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1557.md), the proof appendices included. Held as what the authors show: an index theorem in elastic susceptibilities that holds with prestress and heterogeneous stiffness, whose counts by Theorem 1 always equal the classical ones; zero-displacement tensions that are the states of self-stress; forces exciting the zero modes that follow the symmetry of geometry and energy together; and, on two worked networks with uniform stiffness, prestress that redirects and localizes those forces with the mechanisms unchanged. It is a linear theory: it does not say when prestress makes a structure rigid, nor whether zero modes extend to finite motions. Whether an independent derivation confirms it is [QUESTION-423](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-423.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1415](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1415.md) v2 | Kresling stacks are Preisach memories | Jules, Reid, Daniels, Mungan and Lechenault (2022), [LIT-2072](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2072.md), read in [NOTE-1617](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1617.md). Shown in experiment on one four-barrel stack and its softer twin, with the Preisach graph confirmed and defect states found by twisting by hand. It does not say that the 64 counted states were all observed (39 of 48 single-defect states were), that the readout identifies every state, or that loading alone can create a defect in a decoupled stack. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1417](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1417.md) v3 | Prestress tunes Kresling barriers and sequences | Zang, Zhao, Misseroni & Paulino (2025), [LIT-2091](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2091.md), read in [NOTE-1569](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1569.md) (the main text; the SI was not read). Held as what one group's model and prototypes showed, with three-cell assemblies and a theory that misses the panel buckling seen in experiment. The "frustration" is prestress applied from outside, stored elastic energy, not an incompatibility inside the crease pattern. Of 56 ordered transitions in the three-cell stack, prestress opens the 8 blocked by the ordering of the barriers; the 16 that need intermediate states stay unachievable. | Active |
| [THEORY-1418](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1418.md) v3 | Distractor branches grow with boundary length | Stern, Pinson & Murugan (2017), [LIT-2074](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2074.md), read from the arXiv v1 preprint in [NOTE-1571](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1571.md); the published version and the SI were not read. Its limits: simulations on idealized rigid-panel vertices with zero-temperature descent, actuation statistics from one 4 × 4 pattern, and folding islands offered as a heuristic, not a necessary and sufficient condition. The authors limit the difficulty to the flat state. The analogy to SAT and protein folding carries no hardness proof. | Active |
| [THEORY-1419](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1419.md) v2 | Self-stress decides if counting predicts rigidity | Damavandi, Hagh, Santangelo and Manning (2022; arXiv 2021), [LIT-2041](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2041.md), read in full in [NOTE-1570](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1570.md). Proposed: a single paper's derivations, with the hardest case left open by the authors. It does not say that a system with states of self-stress is never energetically rigid, nor that the shear modulus measures rigidity; and it covers Hookean energies only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1420](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1420.md) v3 | Persistent homology extends disconnectivity graphs | Mirth, Zhai, Bush, Alvarado, Jordan, Heim, Krishnamoorthy, Pflaum, Clark, Zhang and Adams (2021), [LIT-2047](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2047.md), read in [NOTE-1616](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1616.md), appendices with the full proofs skimmed. The first two parts are standard correspondences the paper states and illustrates; the closed form is its Theorems 1 and 2. It treats one scalar energy only: nothing here covers several resources at once, which would need multi-parameter persistence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1423](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1423.md) v2 | Positive-curvature vertex splits near flat | Berry, Lee-Trimble and Santangelo (2020), [LIT-2024](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2024.md), read in full in [NOTE-1605](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1605.md) (arXiv v1). Active on its reading (ADR-065); whether the result holds is THEORY-1526's. The single-vertex result follows from the second-order condition hᵀQh = K, whose proof to quadratic order the authors call somewhat involved, and is confirmed numerically on one symmetric 5-fold vertex. It does not say anything far from the flat state or at large curvature, it does not hold when faces may pass through each other, and its multi-vertex extension is conditional. | Active |
| [THEORY-1425](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1425.md) | Pruning ~1% of bonds tunes network response | Rocks, Pashine, Bischofberger, Goodrich, Liu and Nagel (2017; arXiv 2016), [LIT-2060](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2060.md), read in [NOTE-1607](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1607.md) from the arXiv v1 preprint; the PNAS text was not reached. Proposed for that reason and because the Supporting Information was not read. It is a linear, athermal result for central-force networks made rigid first: it does not say why the chosen bonds work, that the network could find them itself, or that allostery in proteins works this way. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1427](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1427.md) v3 | Flat triangulated origami traps misfolds | Chen and Santangelo (2018), [LIT-2021](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2021.md), read in [NOTE-1614](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1614.md) (main text in full, appendices skimmed). The title keeps the source's hedges: the count of 2^Vi branches is numerical for Vi from 2 to 8 and proven only for H1 triangulations, which are rare; second-order solutions are treated as configurations without a general guarantee; and only patterns with four boundary vertices are treated. It does not say how the branches join away from the flat state, or that a real sheet misfolds at any measured rate. | Active |
| [THEORY-1428](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1428.md) v3 | Miura-ori soft modes are edge modes | Evans, Silverberg & Santangelo (2015), [LIT-2070](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2070.md), read in full in [NOTE-1587](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1587.md) from the arXiv v2 source, with the step from J0 and D(q) to the dispersion relation and decay length checked. Active as a report of what the theory predicts. A linear theory about one ground state, with facet bending coarse-grained as folds, checked on one 8 × 8 paper sheet, with the decay length for a pop-through defect estimated only to within 100%. Registered as a stand-in for Silverberg et al. (2014); it does not carry that paper's claims of bistable cells or crystal-like defects. Whether another group's test agrees is [QUESTION-447](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-447.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1431](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1431.md) v2 | Multistable origami can be a reservoir computer | Liu, Fang, Xu and Wang (2023), [LIT-2026](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2026.md), read in [NOTE-1600](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1600.md). The comparison with the raw inputs (90.4% against 87.2% on binarized MNIST) and the memory result are simulations with a least-action model; the experiment covers ten 5×4-pixel digits on a 4×2-cell prototype. It does not say that the material learns: only the linear readout is trained. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1433](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1433.md) v2 | Compliant mechanisms via topological derivative | Krishnakumar and Suresh (2015), [LIT-2099](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2099.md), read in full in [NOTE-1582](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1582.md) from a lab-posted manuscript, as a stand-in for Sigmund (1997). Proposed: hinge-freedom is shown by pictures of a handful of coarse-mesh designs, and the η trade-off on one example. It is the authors' account of their own method, not of Sigmund's; it does not say that the designs stay hinge-free under stress constraints or large deformation, or that they were built. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1437](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1437.md) v3 | Origami staples bind fully once started | Cumberworth and Reinhardt (2025), [LIT-2121](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2121.md), read in full in [NOTE-1626](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1626.md) from the submitted version. Active as a report of the review's synthesis of coarse-grained simulations, mostly the authors' own, of small 2D designs. The authors note evidence that staples do not bind fully once started in a larger 3D-lattice-based design, and that their lattice model's loop costs are fixed only up to a constant. The experimental evidence on origami hysteresis they report is mixed. Whether experiment bears the account out is [QUESTION-445](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-445.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1438](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1438.md) | DNA origami joints give one designed DOF | Marras, Zhou, Su and Castro (2015), [LIT-2118](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2118.md), read in [NOTE-1635](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1635.md) (main text and figure captions; the Supporting Information unread). Proposed: the conformational statistics are negative-stain TEM fractions on a surface, which the authors call upper bounds, over 52 to 918 particles with misfolds excluded, and one actuation cycle is reported. It does not say that the mechanisms fold with high yield, that switching survives repeated cycles, or that the grid fractions are those in solution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1439](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1439.md) | Staple choice steers degenerate origami folds | Dunn, Dannenberg, Ouldridge, Kwiatkowska, Turberfield and Bath (2015), [LIT-2135](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2135.md), read in [NOTE-1643](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1643.md). The shift is shown by AFM shape counts on one tile, one anneal ramp and one buffer, with 36-62% of candidate objects fitted; the trapping figure (52% misfolds with full seams, 1% with broken ones) is the model's. The equal stability of the final folds is the authors' design argument, not a measurement, and the model is not thermodynamically self-consistent. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1440](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1440.md) v3 | 3D origami folds in a narrow 5 °C window | Sobczak (2018), LIT-2138, read in NOTE-1644 (Chapter 3 in full), standing in for Sobczak, Martin, Gerling and Dietz (2012), [LIT-2131](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2131.md), whose abstract says the same in kind. Measured by gel and SYBR Green assays, mostly on one brick family. Persistence and non-formation are each measured, on two-hour and 48-hour scales, but not paired at one temperature; the brick's melting temperature appears only in a figure. | Active |
| [THEORY-1441](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1441.md) v2 | Scaffold topology sets staple binding order | Schneider, Möritz and Dietz (2019), [LIT-2122](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2122.md), read in [NOTE-1641](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1641.md). One object, one temperature and one buffer; progress normalized per reaction, so the delay is in when signals saturate, not in a measured yield; the single-terminus kinetics come from a model that assumes the independence it reports. It does not say that topology alone sets the order: the authors' Results call local sequence and connectivity "two important factors". | Active |
| [THEORY-1442](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1442.md) v2 | Staple concentration moves nucleation site | Lee Tin Wah, David, Rudiuk, Baigl and Estévez-Torres (2016), [LIT-2137](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2137.md), read in [NOTE-1625](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1625.md) (main text and supplement). Active as a report; its limits: one design, one lab, the two concentration changes made together with a slower ramp. The title asserts where folding starts under each allocation and the authors' attribution; it does not assert that the final object or its yield is unchanged, that a fixed stock was reallocated, or that the mechanism is established. | Active |
| [THEORY-1443](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1443.md) v2 | Only a base probe detects missing staples | Wagenbauer, Wachauf and Dietz (2014), [LIT-2128](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2128.md), read in [NOTE-1637](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1637.md). The indistinguishability under TEM and gel mobility is shown directly; the residual counts are extrapolations from a calibration that assumes each omitted staple adds exactly its own bases unpaired, with a background floor near the best result. It does not say how defects are spread across particles, nor anything about misfolds that leave bases paired. | Active |
| [THEORY-1444](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1444.md) v2 | Multilayer origami needs long anneals, low yield | Douglas, Dietz, Liedl, Högberg, Graf and Shih (2009), [LIT-2130](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2130.md), read in [NOTE-1629](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1629.md) (main text and captions; the Supplementary Information unread). Active as a report; its limits: per-target yields and the six-helix-bundle data are in the unread supplement, yield is a gel-band fraction and quality is judged by eye. The title asserts the reported conditions and outcomes; it does not assert the authors' conjecture that multilayer structures traverse harder kinetic traps, nor any mechanism for the cation effects. | Active |
| [THEORY-1445](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1445.md) v2 | Free-energy staple breaks raise origami yield | Aksel, Navarro, Fong and Douglas (2024), [LIT-2125](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2125.md), read in [NOTE-1642](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1642.md). The yields are integrated gel intensity in a hand-bounded window after one 21 h anneal, with no stated replicates and TEM only of the redesigns; the correlation is R² = 0.86 over 8 designs from the same four structures. The largest gain (10×10, 2 to 61%) also changed the scaffold seam and paired fraction. The score is equilibrium and ignores folding kinetics and inter-staple cooperativity, so the account is one of more stable parts, not of a chosen pathway. | Active |
| [THEORY-1446](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1446.md) v2 | Origami defects track loop-entropy skew | Majikes, Hasni, Haridas, Robertson, Pintar, Zwolak and Liddle (2026), [LIT-2127](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2127.md), read in [NOTE-1639](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1639.md). Defectivity is a class-weighted AFM proxy for missing or blocked staples, useful for comparison only; the combination is fitted on 28 designs of one shape, with linear models, and a LASSO over more metrics swaps the blocking term for positive inter-domain cooperativity. The poor-anneal conditions are argued, in supplementary sections not read here, to preserve the ordering seen under standard anneals. The authors' reading that 2D origami assembly is funnel-like rather than path-like is their interpretation of the fit. | Active |
| [THEORY-1447](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1447.md) v2 | Staple cooperativity makes asymmetric hysteresis | Dannenberg, Dunn, Bath, Kwiatkowska, Turberfield and Ouldridge (2015), [LIT-2129](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2129.md), read in [NOTE-1645](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1645.md). A simulation of one 166-domain tile, with parameters chosen to match the scale of hysteresis in one SYBR Green experiment. It does not say that origami has alternative stable states or kinetic traps: the model has a unique equilibrium at each temperature and no misbinding, and its hysteresis shrinks with slower ramps. | Active |
| [THEORY-1448](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1448.md) v2 | Templating raises tile sticky-end concentration | Ni, Zhou, Zhu, Bershadsky, Ai, Wang, Sha, Seeman and Chaikin (2026), [LIT-2124](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2124.md), read in [NOTE-1630](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1630.md). The effective-concentration figure is the model's estimate, with a FRET fit of about 0.2 mM; the 2 °C agreement is over assemblies up to tetramers; the replication rates are one figure whose definition is in a supplementary figure not read. The paper's predicted upper limit on string melting temperature, and with it the feasibility of replicating very large patterns, is extrapolation; in experiment tetramers barely separated before the tiles unravelled. | Active |
| [THEORY-1449](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1449.md) v2 | Faster-growing mutant dominates DNA replicator | Zhou, Sha, Ni, Seeman and Chaikin (2021), [LIT-2126](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2126.md), read in [NOTE-1628](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1628.md), as the stand-in for He et al. (2017), [LIT-2132](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2132.md), whose replicator it extends. The 3.5% is computed from a 16% per-monomer mismatch rate measured by AFM counts; the takeover is one run of 13 cycles counted by AFM, with the fit's equations and per-cycle rates in an SI not read. Fitness here is assigned by the recognition-strand design, and monomers, temperatures and UV are supplied every cycle, so it says nothing of a population that maintains its own conditions. | Active |
| [THEORY-1450](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1450.md) v3 | Aptamer AND gate opens DNA barrel | Douglas, Bachelet and Church (2012), [LIT-2136](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2136.md), read in [NOTE-1634](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1634.md) (main text and captions; the Supporting Online Material, with the lock-length data, unread). Active as a report; its limits: one lab, a proof of principle, conformations read by TEM counts and flow cytometry. The title asserts the gate and the lock-length dependence; it does not assert that the device can revise its rule, which it cannot, nor anything about cycling, holding costs or clinical use. | Active |
| [THEORY-1451](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1451.md) v2 | Block proofreading cuts tile assembly errors | Winfree and Bekbolatov (2004), [LIT-2119](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2119.md), read in [NOTE-1640](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1640.md) from the authors' submitted preprint. Simulation and kinetic-trap theory, with trap rates fitted and no rigorous proof. It does not say that proofreading has been shown in DNA, that its gain is exponential in practice, or that it corrects every error: growth on facets, nucleation of boundaries and implementation errors are outside it. | Active |
| [THEORY-1452](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1452.md) v2 | Staple pools let DNA origami self-heal | Scheckenbach, Schubert, Forthmann, Glembockyte and Tinnefeld (2021), [LIT-2139](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2139.md), read in [NOTE-1636](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1636.md) from the main text; the Supporting Information, which holds the toehold experiments and the 10% serum data, was not read. It does not say that origami repairs itself without supply, that nuclease damage is shown to expose toeholds, or that repair restores every damaged structure: missing staples were replaced in about half. | Active |
| [THEORY-1453](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1453.md) v2 | Origami nucleation barrier set by stacking | Cumberworth, Frenkel and Reinhardt (2022), [LIT-2134](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2134.md), read in [NOTE-1638](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1638.md). Equilibrium simulation of four designs of at most 27 domains with averaged energies. It does not say that a barrier changes folding times or yields, which are not simulated, nor that it causes the hysteresis seen in temperature ramps, which the authors explain but do not reproduce, nor that larger designs have no other barriers. | Active |
| [THEORY-1454](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1454.md) v2 | Anchored folds are stabler; distance costs | Majikes, Patrone, Schiffels, Zwolak, Kearsley, Forry and Liddle (2020), [LIT-2117](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2117.md), read in [NOTE-1632](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1632.md) (main text, captions and tables; the supplement unread). Active as a report; its limits: one fold and one melt domain, measured on the melt only, with equilibrium assumed and not tested. The title asserts the measurement and that the authors infer the pathway; it does not assert the pathway, which the authors say needs systems with multiple folds, nor anything about hysteresis, kinetics or whole-origami yield. | Active |
| [THEORY-1455](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1455.md) v2 | Best-scored scaffold folded worst | Shirt-Ediss, Torelli, Navarro, Khamis, Kaplan, Trewby, Elezgaray, Moradzadeh, Haydell, Keppner, Famulok, Armstrong and Krasnogor (2026), [LIT-2123](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2123.md), read in [NOTE-1627](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1627.md). The ordering of best against worst is shown for four shapes with one off-target-prone exemplar each, replicated in a second lab for two; the de Bruijn control did not always win. Trapping is the authors' hypothesis: aggregation is seen, no trap is located, and GC content and synthesis route are not controlled. The wording of the title is the reader's. | Active |
| [THEORY-1456](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1456.md) v2 | Scaffold and staples fold arbitrary DNA shapes | Rothemund (2006), [LIT-2120](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2120.md), read in [NOTE-1631](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1631.md). The folding is demonstrated; the yields are judged fractions of AFM fields with small counts that mix folding with deposition and tip damage; the mechanism is the author's argument. It does not say that the folded shape is the equilibrium state, nor anything about folding temperature, kinetics or hysteresis, which were not measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-1457](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1457.md) v2 | Excess staples block folds past a turnover | Majikes, Patrone, Kearsley, Zwolak and Liddle (2021), [LIT-2133](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2133.md), read in [NOTE-1633](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1633.md) (main text, captions and tables; the supplement, with the slower-anneal control, unread). Active as a report; its limits: one lab, one fold at a time, one reporter channel that cannot tell blocked from unbound, and one fold distance declared anomalous by assumption. The title asserts the single-fold measurement and that the authors propose the whole-origami escape; it does not assert the escape, nor that the blocked state is a kinetic trap. | Active |
| [THEORY-1464](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1464.md) v3 | One hatchery generation lowers wild fitness | Christie, Marine, French & Blouin (2012), [LIT-2185](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2185.md), main text read in [NOTE-1652](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1652.md); the SI was not read. Active as a report of what the authors show, with the hedge that the hatchery advantage is significant only with 1995 excluded; one population, and the per-year results and the 1995 release details rest on SI tables not read. It does not identify the traits selected, does not show crowding is the pressure (one year), and does not say other taxa respond as fast. | Active |
| [THEORY-1467](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1467.md) v3 | Translocation amid threats sustains reliance | Mussmann et al. (2017), [LIT-2183](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2183.md), read in [NOTE-1670](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1670.md), and filed as a stand-in for the unread Scott et al. (2010), [LIT-2146](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2146.md), on the concept of conservation reliance. Twenty years after translocations, Illinois greater prairie chickens are small, declining and inbred, with no sign of genetic rescue; the authors argue that supply without relief of the habitat threat perpetuates reliance, and that "both must be alleviated in tandem". Active as a report of what the authors argue; one population, and the threshold is a conceptual figure, not a measured one. | Active |
| [THEORY-1478](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1478.md) v3 | Captive-bred releases decline on average | Morris, Brook, Moseby & Johnson (2021), [LIT-2163](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2163.md), read as its EcoEvoRxiv preprint in [NOTE-1657](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1657.md). Reported success: captive 76.0%, wild 70.2%; soft 79.8%, hard 75.0%. Growth: captive −2.8, wild +2.2; soft −1.3, hard +5.6. Active as a report of what the review measured; the preprint, not the published version, was read; the source and release contrasts are raw group means with large spreads in a growth subset of 87, not adjusted contrasts; and the soft-release result runs against the abstract of Resende et al. (2021), [LIT-2173](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2173.md), unread. | Active |
| [THEORY-1482](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1482.md) v4 | Kirtland's warbler stays conservation-reliant | Brown et al. (2019), [LIT-2155](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2155.md), read in [NOTE-1674](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1674.md), and filed as a stand-in for the unread Scott et al. (2010), [LIT-2146](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2146.md), on whether conservation reliance ends at recovery. In a 100-year viability model the population holds at about 2,500 males under current management and stabilizes at about 1,900 or 1,300 males when the planted habitat is cut; "loss of breeding habitat alone (up to 48.7%) did not cause extinction". The sharp edges: a single-sex model whose ceiling density dependence builds in that population tracks habitat, with no scenario ending the supply. | Active |
| [THEORY-1489](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1489.md) v3 | Hawaiian waterbirds need perpetual management | Underwood et al. (2013), [LIT-2153](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2153.md), read in [NOTE-1672](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1672.md), and filed as a stand-in for the unread Scott et al. (2010), [LIT-2146](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2146.md), on the kinds of ongoing management and their perpetuity. Twenty years of counts show the three species stable or rising, with managed refuges holding 34–42 % of each population on about 15 % of the wetland; the authors hold that "without perpetual active management of wetlands in Hawai'i, the endangered waterbird species likely would experience population declines". The sharp edges: the trends are observed, but the decline without management is asserted from one marsh and cited studies, with no unmanaged control. | Active |
| [THEORY-1495](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1495.md) v4 | Hatchery fish are less fit in the wild | Araki, Berejikian, Ford & Blouin (2008), [LIT-2192](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2192.md), read in full in [NOTE-1668](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1668.md). The sharp edges: the review is of 14 studies, nine on steelhead, with low power below a 10–15% difference, and the model is one generation and one trait. The >30% target is the paper's reading of the Hood River result, which it also gives as about 30% and 30–40%, and which the Science abstract gives as about 40%; this does not settle which. It does not say that hatcheries cannot raise numbers, that local broodstock prevents the loss, or that the mechanism was measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-1500](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1500.md) | Kerr solitons exist in a detuning window | Herr, Brasch, Jost, Wang, Kondratiev, Gorodetsky and Kippenberg (2014), [LIT-2204](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2204.md), read in [NOTE-1692](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1692.md) from arXiv v3; experiment in one MgF2 resonator, simulation of the coupled-mode (Lugiato-Lefever) equations without thermal effects, and approximate analytics. Proposed: the window rests on an infinite-domain analysis the record has not read, and the equations were read from a page image because extraction drops square roots. It does not say that formation shows hysteresis (no reverse sweep is reported), how fast a soliton vanishes after switch-off (not measured), or how the number of solitons varies between experimental runs (reported for simulations only). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1501](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1501.md) | Solitons survive collisions unchanged | Zabusky & Porter (2010), [LIT-2208](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2208.md), read in full in [NOTE-1689](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1689.md), an encyclopedia article by the co-author of the 1965 letter. Filed as the read neighbour of Zabusky & Kruskal (1965), which was not reached. The definition is the article's, after Scott (2005); the collision property is illustrated by the article's own simulation, not proved there; the history is Zabusky's later account of his own work. It holds for integrable equations: the article says the relatives do not in general share the interaction property. The wording is the filer's, from the reader's report; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1502](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1502.md) v2 | Only sine-Gordon breathers are exactly periodic | Fodor (2019), [LIT-2197](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2197.md), read in [NOTE-1698](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1698.md) (Chapter 2, the introduction and the summary). What the review derives: the family result, the exponentially small leading-order radiation (checked by two independent computations, by Segur and Kruskal's earlier value for φ4, and by numerics that approach it as the amplitude falls), and the dimension dependence of stability from the core energy. A neighbour of Copeland, Gleiser & Müller (1995), [LIT-2200](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2200.md), whose sudden end it generalizes. The wider statement, that every state but the sine-Gordon breather radiates and that 3+1 oscillons last a few thousand oscillations at most, is [THEORY-1555](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1555.md). Whether fine-tuned resonant oscillons are permanent is left open. | Active |
| [THEORY-1504](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1504.md) v2 | Dissipative solitons are single attractors | Grelu and Akhmediev (2012), [LIT-2196](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2196.md), read in full in [NOTE-1688](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1688.md) from the authors' manuscript on HAL. Held as a report of what the source holds, its truth left to THEORY-1548; the caveats: the review states the account and cites the simulations and experiments behind it without reproducing them. Its contrast with conservative solitons is with the integrable case; it does not say that a dissipative soliton exists only above a pump threshold, or that it is bistable or hysteretic. | Active |
| [THEORY-1506](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1506.md) | Bubbles settle into long-lived oscillons | Copeland, Gleiser & Müller (1995), [LIT-2200](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2200.md), read in full in [NOTE-1699](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1699.md). Shown by numerical simulation, with a one-degree-of-freedom Gaussian ansatz explaining the lower radius bound and the end; spherical symmetry throughout, stability tested only against radial perturbations. It does not explain the upper radius bound, give an analytic lifetime, or define the plateau's endpoints formally. The wording of the title is the reader's condensation of the paper's §§III–IV and VII. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1507](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1507.md) v2 | Topological charge bounds soliton energy | Tong (2005), [LIT-2207](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2207.md), read in NOTE-1694 for the topological charge and the kinks (§1.1, §2.1, §§3.1–3.2, §3.8.3, §§4.1–4.3.2). Standard topological soliton theory, stated by Tong for instantons, monopoles, vortices and domain walls in gauge theories. The thesis that a topological soliton cannot decay except by annihilation with an opposite charge or by a change at the boundary is the reader's inference from these points, not Tong's statement, and is not part of this account. A neighbour of Copeland, Gleiser & Müller (1995), [LIT-2200](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2200.md), for the protection oscillons lack. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1509](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1509.md) v2 | Damped solitons shrink and shed a shelf | Grimshaw, Smyth & Stepanyants (2018), [LIT-2198](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2198.md), read in full in [NOTE-1687](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1687.md), for the Benjamin–Ono equation with six kinds of weak loss, by first-order adiabatic theory checked against direct numerics. Filed as the read neighbour of Kivshar & Malomed (1989), whose central method for damped solitons it carries in one equation. The KdV laws, which make the title's "integrable wave equation" more than one case, are quoted in the paper from earlier work, not derived, and so are not shown here. It says nothing of NLS, of gain or supply, or of strong loss. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1511](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1511.md) v3 | Controlled ventilation weakens the diaphragm | Jaber, Jung, Matecki & Petrof (2011), [LIT-2211](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2211.md), read in [NOTE-1702](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1702.md), standing in for Levine et al. (2008), [LIT-2212](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2212.md), whose abstract only was read. A review: the human evidence is small case-control biopsy series in brain-dead donors and observational twitch-pressure measurements, so the numbers here are the review's restatement of studies not read; the pectoralis control is Levine's alone; the evidence on partial support is animal. It does not show that the loss causes failed weaning, or whether and how fast the diaphragm recovers. | Active |
| [THEORY-1512](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1512.md) v2 | Most patients can stop ventilation abruptly | Alía & Esteban (2000), [LIT-2215](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2215.md), read in [NOTE-1701](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1701.md), standing in for Boles et al. (2007), [LIT-2213](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2213.md), on the trials behind its recommendations on abrupt and gradual withdrawal. A narrative review by a trialist; the trials themselves were not read. The abstract says SIMV is the most effective method after failed trials, the body that it is the least; the title follows the body and the trials as summarized, and the 2006 correction was not read. It does not settle pressure support against T-tube trials, on which the two trials disagree. | Active |
| [THEORY-1513](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1513.md) v2 | Steroid adrenal suppression is common | Broersen, Pereira, Jørgensen and Dekkers (2015), [LIT-2214](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2214.md), read in [NOTE-1703](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1703.md) from the reprint in Broersen's 2019 thesis, supplements unread. Held as what the study finds, with its hedges: the pooled shares are from 74 observational articles at high risk of bias, with no individual-patient data, and the dose and duration gradients are crude strata in asthma patients of all routes. It does not say that longer use means longer recovery: the two retest groups differ in regimen and interval together. Figure 4 labels the 6-month retest as after 4 weeks. The paper has no taper data; its verdict on withdrawal schemes is cited from Dinsen et al. 2013. | Active |
| [THEORY-1514](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1514.md) v4 | Ventilate to quiet-breathing diaphragm effort | Goligher et al. (2020), [LIT-2216](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2216.md), read in [NOTE-1704](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1704.md). A consensus-style review: the atrophy side rests on biopsy and ultrasound studies (Levine et al. 2008, [LIT-2212](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2212.md), among them), the injury side is a hypothesis the authors say needs confirmation, the effort target is "probably optimal" from physiology, and no trial of the approach had reported. Its figure of 64% weak after 24 h is weakness on ICU admission, not loss caused by ventilation. | Active |
| [THEORY-1515](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1515.md) v2 | Breathing trials test readiness to wean | Shah, Hart & Kaltsakas (2024), [LIT-2217](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2217.md), read in [NOTE-1706](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1706.md), standing in for Boles et al. (2007), [LIT-2213](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2213.md), whose abstract only was read. A narrative review: the classification and the definition of failure are restated from the consensus, the frequencies and outcomes are from later cohorts (WIND, WEAN SAFE, Jeong et al. 2015), and the gradient of outcomes across groups is partly definitional. It does not say why some patients cannot be weaned, nor that ventilation itself causes the failure. | Active |
| [THEORY-1516](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1516.md) v3 | Glucocorticoids invariably suppress the HPA axis | Beuschlein et al. (2024), [LIT-2218](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2218.md), read in [NOTE-1705](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1705.md) from the open copy on Europe PMC, supplementary GRADE tables unread. (2015) and three later low-quality cohorts; the taper schedule is graded good clinical practice and the no-taper threshold very-low evidence. The thesis says "it was proven that these spaces embody all possible solutions" (abstract). Its uniqueness argument is by example, though it follows from screw reciprocity; finiteness is "suggested" by the six-constraint bound; and the 26 come from a case analysis (chs. 7–8). Proposed until an independent derivation or classification confirms them. The uniqueness half is close to standard linear algebra and might be split off as demonstrated, if a reviewer writes it out. | Proposed |

What the review derives is [THEORY-1502](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1502.md), which this extends. Filed by the twenty-ninth status review as the wider thesis of [THEORY-1502](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1502.md)'s old title ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md), kind 1), with the old title and condition word for word. | Proposed |
