The thesis offers its chart as "a comprehensive classification of screw systems" (§2.1), derives it by a case analysis (Appendix A) that defers to the master's thesis for the 2-DOF column and the column symmetry, and does not compare it type by type with Gibson and Hunt's or Rico and Duffy's classifications. The actuation theory has one bench experiment, whose measured errors were much larger than predicted, and the thesis states that placement is computed from stiffness without saying that the freedom space alone leaves it open. Proposed until an independent classification and a second test exist. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1576](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1576.md) v2 | Transgenerational inheritance is rare in mammals | Heard and Martienssen (2014), read from the accepted manuscript ([NOTE-1254](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1254.md)). The definition the later debate uses, and the mechanistic case against germline transmission in mammals. Human evidence is examined only for nutrition; trauma, Överkalix and the Holocaust studies are not discussed. It fixes the line [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md)'s germline route must cross. | Active |
| [THEORY-1587](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1587.md) v3 | Rodent trauma passes via sperm RNA | Jawaid and Mansuy (2019), a short review from the laboratory behind the MSUS mouse model ([NOTE-1296](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1296.md)). The proponents' side of [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md)'s germline route, which concedes the disputed steps. It does not engage the sceptics, mention germline reprogramming, or report effect sizes, and its own table calls the human studies intergenerational. | Active |
| [THEORY-1593](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1593.md) v2 | Hunger Winter conception lowers IGF2 methylation | Heijmans et al. (2008), read from the reprint in Tobi's thesis ([NOTE-1248](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1248.md)). One locus, one tissue, one cohort, one sample per person. The exposure is the person's own, around their own conception, and no later generation is measured: this is the womb route of [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md), not inheritance, and from famine, not psychological trauma. | Active |
| [THEORY-1594](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1594.md) v2 | POW fathers' sons died earlier in old age | Costa, Yetter and DeSomer (2018), read from the PMC text without the SI Appendix ([NOTE-1255](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1255.md)). The best human paternal case [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md) holds: large, with two natural controls, but the within-family estimate has P = 0.056, maternal nutrition is inferred from season, and the mechanism is argued by elimination, with no data on parenting. | Active |
| [THEORY-1596](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1596.md) v2 | Grandparental diet tracks grandchild mortality | Pembrey, Saffery and Bygren (2014), a position paper of the Network in Epigenetic Epidemiology, read in place of Pembrey et al. 2006 ([NOTE-1320](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1320.md)). About 100 probands per cohort, one population, no measured family culture, and priors partly set after earlier results. It corrects [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md)'s label: Överkalix is a male-line nutritional case, in which good supply, not poor, went with higher grandchild mortality, and the authors leave the mechanism open. | Active |
| [THEORY-1602](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1602.md) v3 | Paternal odour fear passes as odour sensitivity | Dias and Ressler (2014), read in full ([NOTE-1281](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1281.md)). The best animal case for [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md)'s germline route, and narrower than it is cited for: cue-specific sensitivity, not inherited fear. IVF offspring were tested for anatomy only, cross-fostering was done on the maternal line only, and the proposed sperm mark rests on groups as small as four. [QUESTION-302](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-302.md) cites it for where an insect's learned aversion would pass to offspring. | Active |
| [THEORY-1612](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1612.md) v2 | Evidence accumulates for inherited trauma marks | Youssef et al. (2018), a short narrative review read in place of Yehuda et al. 2016 ([NOTE-1310](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1310.md)). It uses "transgenerational" for any parent-to-child effect, and its conclusion outruns its evidence: no study it reviews separates transmission from shared or in-utero exposure. For [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md) it corrects a label: the FKBP5 study is intergenerational, and the child does not carry the parent's mark. | Active |
| [THEORY-1614](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1614.md) v2 | No validated route to inherited epigenomes | Bird (2024), a Perspective ([NOTE-1264](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1264.md)). The only one of the record's three sceptical readings to name the human trauma studies. It does not separate inter- from transgenerational effects, and it cites a larger Swedish cohort only for its failure to replicate, not for the effects that cohort's title reports. Bird has written with Horsthemke and commented on Heard's manuscript, so the three are one school. | Active |
| [THEORY-1618](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1618.md) v2 | Human epigenetic inheritance can hardly be proven | Horsthemke (2018), a Comment ([NOTE-1265](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1265.md)). A design argument, not a finding: it explains why [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md)'s test of separating the germline from uterine, parenting and cultural routes cannot yet be run in humans. Its view that cultural transmission outweighs epigenetic inheritance is stated as opinion, with no evidence for the comparison. | Active |
| [THEORY-1621](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1621.md) v2 | Child survivors' daughters showed no difference | Fridman (2011), a Leiden PhD thesis read in place of its promotors' meta-analyses ([NOTE-1291](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1291.md)). Small (32 survivors, 33 comparisons, 79 daughters), with selective attrition and daughters recruited for having an infant. It also restates the meta-analyses, at second hand and without effect sizes: no second- or third-generation traumatization in non-clinical samples with adequate designs. The parenting route of [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md), tested with the identity route held fixed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1652](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1652.md) | OTOF therapy makes infant genetic testing needed | Reisinger and Cederroth, read in [NOTE-1801](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1801.md) (Read). Comments on the FDA's approval (announced 23 April 2026) of Regeneron's Otarmeni, the first gene therapy for a genetic hearing loss (DFNB9, OTOF), and on convergent results from other programmes. Because the therapy is gene-specific and time-sensitive, infants with bilateral hearing loss need genetic diagnosis; clinical sequences should change so that children with profound loss and intact otoacoustic emissions get a genetic diagnosis before a cochlear implant. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1654](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1654.md) | Microchimerism is bidirectional and long-lived | Chua and colleagues' consensus of 29 microchimerism researchers ([LIT-2415](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2415.md), read in [NOTE-1768](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1768.md)). The established half is what the owner's link to graded individuality needs as a premise; the open half is why it cannot yet carry more. Proposed because the established half rests on primary studies not read here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1658](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1658.md) | LysM+CD11c+ maternal cells sustain tolerance | Peng, Way and colleagues' result as Cincinnati Children's reports it ([LIT-2428](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2428.md), read in [NOTE-1763](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1763.md)). The persistence of foreign-origin cells in a host and their part in the host's regulation come apart: one marked subset does the tolerogenic work, and the rest persist without it. Proposed because the source is a press post and the paper could not be read; the Europe PMC abstract agrees with it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1662](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1662.md) | Brain sickness responses are pathogen-specific | Sullivan et al., read in [NOTE-1775](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1775.md) (Read). In mice, five sterile immune challenges modelling bacterial infection (LPS), viral infection (poly I:C), parasite infection (soluble *Toxoplasma* antigen, STAg), allergy (bee-venom PLA2) and colitis (DSS) produce distinct "sickness states" at three scales: organismal (temperature, food intake, locomotion, metabolism, social behaviour, ultrasonic vocalizations), cellular (whole-brain FOS activity, which a classifier uses to predict the challenge) and molecular (a 940-gene MERFISH atlas of the preoptic and paraventricular hypothalamus). The states cluster: LPS with poly I:C; STAg with DSS; PLA2 apart. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1670](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1670.md) | Ion channels regulate development; how is unclear | George and Bates (2022), Mechanisms Underlying Influence of Bioelectricity in Development, read in [NOTE-1772](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1772.md) (Skimmed). A review of how ion channels and membrane potential (Vmem) act in development: human channelopathies with developmental phenotypes, conserved roles across species, spontaneous calcium oscillations in non-excitable tissue, and the cellular processes (death, proliferation, polarity, migration) and signalling pathways (BMP, Notch, Wnt, Hedgehog) that channels touch. It proposes calcium as the main mediator and a model in which Vmem and calcium oscillations, shaped by mechanical forces, coordinate cells across a tissue. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1673](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1673.md) | Gut microbes contribute to, not cause, disorders | Almarzooqi et al., read in [NOTE-1773](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1773.md) (Skimmed). A narrative review of the microbiota–gut–brain axis (MGBA) in psychiatry, organized around the move "from association to causality". It sets out a graded hierarchy of causal evidence (confounder-controlled association, temporal precedence, experimental necessity/sufficiency, human genetic or interventional validation, cross-cohort replication), reviews mechanisms (immune, HPA, vagal/ENS, barrier), grades the evidence per disorder, and reviews translation (psychobiotics, diet, FMT, biomarkers). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1687](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1687.md) | Fetal microchimeric cells heal maternal wounds | [LIT-2439](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2439.md) neighbour: Castela et al., read in [NOTE-1791](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1791.md) (Read). Fetal microchimeric cells (FMCs) traffic into maternal circulation and persist for decades; on maternal injury they migrate to the site and aid repair. Here, in mice, a reparative FMC subset is CD11b+ CD34+ CD31+ (fetal "MPCs") and highly expresses CCR2. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1688](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1688.md) | Tumours hijack the host's nerves | Neuron–tumor crosstalk in cancer: molecular mechanisms and translational advances (Jia, Zhao, Tang, Xie, Huang, Liang, Yang, Wu, Sun, Kwan, Sun, Xu 2026), read in [NOTE-1758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1758.md) (Skimmed). A narrative review of cancer neuroscience. Tumours recruit nerves (neurotrophins such as NGF and BDNF, axon-guidance cues, perineural invasion) or, in the brain, integrate into existing circuits through tumour–neuron synapses; nerve signalling, chiefly sympathetic norepinephrine through β-adrenergic receptors, then builds an immunosuppressive microenvironment; nerves also reach the tumour through endocrine and metabolic routes, including the transfer of mitochondria from neurons to cancer cells; and cancer pain feeds a loop that raises sympathetic tone. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1691](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1691.md) | Microchimeric cells form an extended immune self | Kinder, Stelzer, Arck and Way, read in [NOTE-1728](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1728.md) (Read). A review arguing that the bidirectional transfer of cells between mother and fetus during pregnancy, and their persistence for decades (fetal cells in mothers: fetal microchimerism, FMC; maternal cells in offspring: maternal microchimerism, MMC), is not accidental but serves reproductive fitness: in mice, maternal microchimeric cells sustain offspring's regulatory T cell tolerance of non-inherited maternal antigens (NIMAs), which protects the offspring's own later pregnancies sired by NIMA-matched males (Kinder et al. 2015, ref. 14), and fetal cells retained in mothers may analogously protect later pregnancies (supported in humans by partner-specific protection against preeclampsia). Microchimeric cells may also replace injured tissue or be targets of alloimmunity resembling autoimmunity; causal roles in humans are mostly unestablished. | Proposed |

(2022), Microbiota-derived metabolites as drivers of gut–brain communication, read in [NOTE-1767](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1767.md) (Skimmed). A review of how gut-microbial metabolites (SCFAs, tryptophan/indole derivatives, bile acids, sulfated phenolics and others) influence brain functions through immune, neural and endocrine routes, arranged by neurological function, with a closing assessment of how far human evidence supports the preclinical picture. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1698](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1698.md) | Bracoviruses are obligate wasp symbionts | Strand and Burke (2012), Polydnaviruses as Symbionts and Gene Delivery Systems, read in [NOTE-1770](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1770.md) (Read). Polydnaviruses (PDVs) are viruses carried by parasitoid wasps. In bracoviruses the provirus sits in every wasp cell; it replicates only in calyx cells of the female ovary, and the virions are injected with the eggs into a caterpillar host, where their genes are expressed but never replicate. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1699](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1699.md) | Fetal cells home to injured maternal hearts | Kara et al., read in [NOTE-1727](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1727.md) (Read). Fetal cells were enriched in injured hearts relative to sham and uninjured controls, located in infarct and peri-infarct zones, and by 3–4 weeks co-expressed markers of cardiomyocytes, smooth muscle and endothelium. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1702](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1702.md) | Maternal dysbiosis linked to pup brain changes | Nakhal et al. (2026), read in [NOTE-1738](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1738.md) (Skimmed). Levin argues that biomedicine's bottom-up, molecular ("hardware") paradigm cannot achieve anatomical control (birth defects, regeneration, cancer, aging) and should be complemented by a top-down program that treats cells and tissues as an "agential material" with memories, goals and problem-solving competencies, i.e. a collective intelligence navigating anatomical, transcriptional and physiological spaces. | [THEORY-1714](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1714.md) | Parasitoids reset host growth via host hormones | Cuny and Poelman (2022), Evolution of koinobiont parasitoid host regulation and consequences for indirect plant defence, read in [NOTE-1756](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1756.md) (Skimmed). Koinobiont parasitoids let the host keep feeding while their larvae develop inside it, and regulate the host's growth: usually arresting it (smaller hosts eating less), sometimes prolonging it (larger hosts eating more), and some species switch with conditions. The regulation is done by injected and secreted factors, and it changes the plant's responses to the parasitized herbivore, so it reaches the wider community. | Proposed |

The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-2010](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2010.md) | Buckled beams ratchet bits one cell per cycle | From the reading of [LIT-2805](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2805.md) in [NOTE-2098](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2098.md). In a chain of buckled polymer beams, bits stored as buckling domains are moved one unit cell per cycle of an applied compression pattern. The wall advances when a mode localized at it, softened by the opposite domain's pressure, goes unstable. The authors call this a topological ratchet and distinguish it from Chern-number pumping, which is ill- defined on their path. Logic gates are simulated only. It is here as information transport by boundaries without learning, against the learned defects of A15 ([LIT-2787](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2787.md)). Its mechanical neighbours are [THEORY-1893](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1893.md) (buckled bistable domains, also only under standing compression) and [THEORY-1408](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1408.md), whose index-protected modes it does not use. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2022](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2022.md) | Defects classified by symmetry class and d − D | From the reading of [LIT-2797](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2797.md) in [NOTE-2124](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2124.md). Teo and Kane (2010), arXiv 1006.0690 (Phys. Rev. B 82, 115120). A unified classification of defects in non-interacting insulators and superconductors. It uses the homotopy class of the Bloch or Bogoliubov–de Gennes Hamiltonian H(k, r) on a surface around the defect, which depends only on the symmetry class and δ = d − D, together with a generalized bulk-boundary correspondence, observed in examples rather than proved, that pairs a nontrivial class with protected gapless modes bound to the defect. In the Jackiw–Rebbi kink, the Jackiw–Rossi vortex and the dislocation, the defect's structural charge fixes the mode invariant. In a disordered weak topological insulator the protected modes outlive the structure that produced them. It is here for the relation between defect topology and bound modes ([CLAIM-606](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md), [CLAIM-694](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-694.md)). It shows these are two topologies of different objects. What is protected is the hosted modes, not the defect's persistence. Skimmed in its NOTE. | Proposed |

Shankar, Souslov, Bowick, Marchetti and Vitelli (2020; v3 2021), arXiv 2010.00364, published in Nature Reviews Physics 4, 380–398 (2022). A review of topology in active matter. It presents topological defects of the order parameter and topologically protected edge modes of waves as "two physically distinct classes of phenomena" that share the mathematics of integer invariants. In active nematics, flows the defects generate make +1/2 defects self-propel and unbind. In active fluids and metamaterials, activity can create the band topology that guarantees edge and interface modes. It is here for [QUESTION-490](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-490.md) and the record's split between defect topology and bound-mode topology. It corroborates that a winding number counts defects net ([CLAIM-694](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-694.md)), and it gives a case of one structure on both the charge route and the supplied route ([CLAIM-606](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md)). Skimmed in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2038](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2038.md) | Kink counts predictable before freeze-out | From the reading of [LIT-2833](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2833.md) in [NOTE-2112](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2112.md). Suzuki, Li and Zurek (2026), Physical Review Letters 137, 157301, DOI 10.1103/fstv-lsvh; arXiv 2508.20347 v2. In simulations of a noisy, overdamped 1D φ⁴ field quenched through its symmetry-breaking transition, a recurrent network (and an LSTM and a Transformer) predicts the number and locations of the final kinks from short windows of the field's evolution near the critical point. That is well before the freeze-out time and while the seeds are exponentially small. The onset of predictability scales with the Kibble–Zurek freeze-out time. It is here because it dates when a future individual becomes determined. Creation (near the critical point) and stabilization (at freeze-out) come apart in time ([QUESTION-281](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md)). It also shows that kink locations are set by history, not by the charge ([CLAIM-694](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-694.md)). Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2040](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2040.md) | Zero Chern numbers can host Floquet edge modes | From the reading of [LIT-2790](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2790.md) in [NOTE-2115](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2115.md). Rudner, Lindner, Berg and Levin (2012; v2 2013), arXiv 1212.3324, published in Physical Review X 3, 031005 (2013). In periodically driven, non-interacting 2D lattices, chiral edge modes can exist when every Floquet band has Chern number zero. Two drives with the same stroboscopic bulk can have opposite edge chirality. It is here for interfaces between dynamically distinguished phases ([QUESTION-378](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-378.md), [QUESTION-490](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-490.md)). The founding letter of self-organized criticality: a critical point "reached by starting far from equilibrium", with the percolation-of-minimal-stability heuristic, the sandpile automaton, and power laws judged by eye over two decades. It states no slow-drive, time-scale or conservation condition. It corroborates [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s bullet that SOC reaches a critical point without outside tuning ([ARG-178](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-178.md)), and its finite-size cutoff, asserted without data, is reproduced in [CLAIM-858](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-858.md) ([ARG-181](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-181.md)). Proposed until the reading is confirmed. | Proposed |
